chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Chicago in the Depression thirties
summary: Plenty of music, little money, still working.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: What was it like in Chicago in the thirties? You talked about how it was in the twenties. How was it in the thirties?
That was during the Depression, but --
There was a lot of music.
There was a lot of music going on.
Roy was down at the Three Deuces.
Roy was down at the Three Deuces. There was a lot of music going on. And Nance was downtown, you know, different places. Lot of bands out South. Wasn't making much money, but you were working.
Yeah, Albert Ammons had a good band out there.
How about sessions, were there many sessions around town? Places where guys would go after hours? Like you were saying in the twenties?
What were some of those places?

Well, this first place I mentioned, at 55th and the el, that was around back in the thirties. That's when Art Tatum was here, and Teddy Wilson, just before Teddy Wilson went to New York. He was still around. Oh, my God, I don't know. Gang of musicians were around, and most everybody was working. You wasn't making much money, making $2.00, $3.00 a night, but you was working, and people was spending money. Especially, you know, the black population. We didn't suffer too much during the Depression, musicians didn't.
No, I know. Musicians seemed to do better then than later, really.
Yeah, cause I raised four daughters during the Depression.
